title: CondoGuard Premium Billing, Payments and Refunds
content:
Billing office rules for the CondoGuard Unit-Owners Policy.

## Installment schedule

Each term is billed on its plan's schedule:

| Plan | Installments | Timing |
|---|---|---|
| annual | 1 | due on the term effective date |
| mortgagee escrow | 1 | due on the term effective date, billed to the mortgagee |
| two-pay | 2 | six calendar months apart |
| quarterly | 4 | three calendar months apart |
| monthly EFT | 12 | monthly |

Each installment after the first is the term premium divided by the number of installments, rounded half-up to the cent, and installment 1 takes the difference. Installments are billed only while the policy is bound, in force, pending cancellation or pending nonrenewal, as the policy record shows.

*Worked bill (hypothetical term premium of 1000.01 USD on a quarterly plan):* 1000.01 divided by 4 is 250.0025, which rounds to 250.00 for installments 2, 3 and 4; together they come to 750.00, and installment 1 takes the difference, 250.01.

## Fees

- The installment fee is the tier's two-pay and quarterly service charge on those plans, and the tier's monthly EFT service charge on monthly EFT, charged on each installment after the first.
- A late fee is charged once per installment still unpaid more than the tier's late-fee grace days after its due date.
- A returned-payment fee is charged once per returned payment.
- None of these fees applies to a term billed to the mortgagee, and a fee whose tier amount is 0.00 is never charged.

## Payments, returned payments and refunds

- Payments apply to the oldest charge first and are recorded with their confirmation or check number exactly as issued.
- A returned payment reverses, in full, the one payment it references.
- A refund is issued only when the premium balance is a credit of at least the tier's refund minimum, and it goes to the payer of the most recent payment.

## Mortgagee changes

A mortgagee change is recorded only with the mortgagee's name and loan number exactly as they appear on the mortgage statement.
